@casarthakahuja #14
Finland is giving Study Visas to Indians up to the age of 50... And people are applying for Masters’ programs, where they can also take their family members and dependents along, and the dependants can also work in Finland while the primary members studies... In fact, the number of students in Finland Masters’ programs have almost doubled in 4 years... So Finland has a number of Masters’ programs taught in the English language across Computers, IT, AI, Data Sciences, Cybersecurity, Healthcare, Business, Engineering... and a lot more... Depending on the program you choose, the annual tuition fee is roughly EUR 12000 to 20000, which is lower than what one spends in the US and UK... and living expenses should be easily EUR 1200 per month... But look at the benefits: - You get an A Permit, which allows you to take up part time work of up to 30 hours per week, or 120 hours per month - Your family members and dependants can take up full time work to support themselves and the family - After your 2 years program, you also get an additional two years to extend in Finland, look for a job or to start a business - You can travel across the Schengen countries for 90 days out of 180 days - And there is no upper limit on when you want to enrol for a masters program If you wish to continue living in Finland though and find a job there after the program, it helps immensely to start learning Finnish on the side from the day you land so that you are ready to communicate till the end of your program. Also, you can’t fund your education only by your family members earning there, you have to show adequate savings to be able to fund your education and support your family... the working bit just helps you not erode all your savings away. #casarthakahuja

@idris_workout2 #28
Why don’t we always train to failure? Research shows that a large portion of the hypertrophy and strength benefits can be achieved when a set is stopped within a few reps of failure, without the higher recovery cost and form breakdown associated with true failure. A range of 1–3 RIR can provide an effective stimulus while helping maintain training quality throughout the session. RIR can also help correct two common mistakes: Some people think every set should be taken to failure, while others always stop at 5+ RIR. RIR = Reps in Reserve It refers to the number of quality reps you could still perform when a set ends. For example, 2 RIR means that after finishing the set, you could still perform 2 clean reps. RIR has a direct relationship with RPE: RPE 8 ≈ 2 RIR RPE 9 ≈ 1 RIR RPE 10 = 0 RIR / Failure They’re essentially two ways of describing the same concept. RIR is often easier for athletes to understand because instead of asking them to rate intensity abstractly, it asks: “How many more reps could you have done?” RIR in the OPT Model Stabilization & Endurance: ~3–5 RIR Hypertrophy: mostly 1–3 RIR Strength: 1–3 RIR on heavy sets 0 RIR: only in rare, planned, and supervised situations RIR can also be used for weekly progression: Week 1 → 3 RIR Week 2 → 2 RIR Week 3 → 1 RIR Then → Deload Combined with the 2-for-2 rule for increasing weight, RIR can create a complete autoregulated progression system. 📚 Source: National Academy of Sports Medicine (NASM) #GymTok #gymfam #trainingtofailure #nycfitness

@nrishaala #59
Taking Cash for Your Property Sale? Watch this first I almost made a huge mistake while selling my Bangalore flat last year. The buyer seemed serious, and said he wanted to pay 30 lakhs in cash. Honestly, for a moment, I considered it too. Registering the property at a lower value, and taking the rest in cash, can save on capital gains tax. But as an NRI, I can’t just sit on 30 lakhs in cash in India. If I deposit it in my bank account, income tax wants to know where it came from. If I give it to a family member to deposit, now they’re in trouble too. And taking it abroad is a completely different legal problem. Here’s what made me walk away completely. If the income tax department pulls this transaction for scrutiny and property deals above a certain value almost always get flagged both me and the buyer pay tax on the same 30 lakhs. He pays tax on it as unexplained income, at a rate far higher than any tax he’d have saved. I pay capital gains on the full actual sale value. We both lose more than we saved. I went back to the buyer and said: just to save 7% stamp duty, you’re going to pay 12.5% capital gains when you sell this flat later, calculated on an understated cost. We split the stamp duty difference and did the entire transaction through banking channels. Elon Musk has predicted how the AI Bubble will burst soon... And to understand his argument, let’s unpack the three constraints that define AI in the world right now... 1/ Electricity Whenever you ask any question to a ChatGPT, Claude or any other model... the query is answered by semiconductor chips at a data centre that run a lot of computational data to give you the answer... and this requires a lot of power... Such that, right now the US is facing a structural problem with electricity... Where China currently generates more electricity than the US, Europe, and India combined... and in the past one year itself, it has added 40% of the entire US grid’s capacity of power... and created the whole US power grid’s capacity in just 4 years... So it is soon on a path to produce almost 4 times the electricity that the US produces in a year... that too with renewables, which are cheaper... Whereas in the US, the proposed new power plants are stuck such that they may take anywhere between 5-12 years to connect to the grid... So the US is about to lose very rapidly to China when it comes to the first constraint or raw material - electricity. 2/ Chips Right now, Nvidia makes the best chips in the world, but the US has put constraints on Nvidia shipping chips to China - where higher tariff would be imposed on chips being pushed to China because they are trying to starve China of access to chips... But quite like ASML makes the machines for creating chips, China has set up a company called SMIC which is already making chips 7 nm small... getting to 5 nm, and would soon reach a point where they can create their equally capable chips as well... 3/ AI Models China’s DeepSeek V4 Flash and Kimi K3 are already very good, and while being ranked in the top 5 models in the world, are already producing US model level output at 10% the cost... #casarthakahuja
